author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Massachusetts has presented Marine veteran T.J. Swenson Jr. with the Madeline “Amy” Sweeney Award for Civilian Bravery for his actions during the May 11 shooting on Memorial Drive in Cambridge. Swenson warned nearby people, directed them toward safety and moved toward the danger as gunfire unfolded, helping protect others until first responders arrived.

Investigators have said Swenson and a Massachusetts state trooper fired at the alleged shooter. Two men were critically injured in the episode but survived. The award recognizes civilians who act without regard for their own safety to assist others, and Swenson’s selection focuses on the immediate steps he took to reduce the risk to people caught near the shooting.

The annual honor is named for Madeline “Amy” Sweeney, an Acton flight attendant aboard American Airlines Flight 11 on September 11, 2001. Sweeney relayed critical information about the hijacking before the plane struck the World Trade Center. Presenting the award on the attack’s 25th anniversary connected Swenson’s response in Cambridge with the award’s broader purpose: recognizing clear-headed assistance during sudden, life-threatening emergencies.
dek: T.J. Swenson Jr. was honored for guiding people away from danger and helping protect them during the May shooting on Memorial Drive in Cambridge.
headline: Marine veteran receives Sweeney civilian-bravery award
